Subject: MAP proposal — Helix capacity & acceptance timeline

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week. Helix would like to formalize a mutual action plan (MAP) that covers capacity reservation (Dedicated vs Private), GPU pool sizing for an initial eval and production ramp, and the acceptance/close milestones so procurement can line up legal and budget. Key asks from our side:

- Clear lead times for Dedicated (Redwood-managed) vs Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Suggested GPU mix for a phased onramp: pilot -> production (we expect 512-token average responses, bursty requests).
- Acceptance criteria and SOC2/compliance gating we should expect.
- Proposed milestone dates so we can coordinate procurement and cloud infra.

I've attached an initial MAP draft (Helix_MAP_Draft.pdf) with our internal timing constraints. Can you share a Redwood-proposed timeline and a short sizing recommendation this week? If it helps, we can do a 30-min MAP handoff on Wed 2/18 — morning PT works best for us.

Thanks,
Laura Benton
Director, AI Platforms
Helix Therapeutics

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP proposal — Helix capacity & acceptance timeline

Laura — thanks for the clear brief and the draft MAP. Looping in Neha (on capacity/onboarding) and Ben (solutions sizing) so we can produce a short, executable MAP. Below is a Redwood-proposed outline and initial sizing assumptions — this is intentionally conservative to give procurement runway.

High-level MAP (proposed)
- Week 0 (Kickoff): MAP signoff, legal handoff start, procurement prerequisites captured.
- Week 1–3 (Evaluation pilot): Dedicated pilot provisioned (smaller tranche) or Private: environment validation (customer infra prep).
- Week 4–8 (Onramp/tranche 1): Production tranche 1 active — steady-state load test & acceptance.
- Week 9–12 (Tranche 2 ramp): Additional capacity (if committed) to hit target pool.

Lead-time estimates (typical)
- Redwood Dedicated (hosted/reserved capacity): 6–8 weeks from signed commitment to fully provisioned H100-equivalent pool (including networking and validation).
- Redwood Private (VPC managed): 8–12 weeks depending on customer networking and KMS setup; on-prem can be 10–16+ weeks (hardware lead times).

Sizing recommendations (pilot -> prod)
- Pilot (proof-of-work): 20–40 A100-equivalent GPUs (enough for 80–200 concurrent sessions at ~512 tokens) — target to validate correctness latency & KV caching.
- Production baseline: 100 A100s (or ~45–60 H100s depending on model + quantization) for a 3x throughput/availability buffer relative to pilot.
- Buffer & staging: Reserve +20% buffer for burst windows; consider hybrid: Dedicated for steady-state + Private for sensitive workloads.

Acceptance gates
- Env readiness: networking, KMS, role-based access confirmed.
- Performance: 99th percentile tail latency < X ms (we'll set exact target per model during pilot).
- Functional: Prompt set / eval coverage pass (we'll share a template).
- Compliance: SOC2 artifacts & audit log access validated (if required for Private).

Attachments: helix-map-v1.docx (proposed MAP with milestones), redwood-leadtimes-summary.pdf (lead-time assumptions).
Related: https://hubspot.com/deal/HLX-2026-038, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcd_example_map_folder

Next steps
- Ben to add sizing calc and risk notes.
- We propose a 30-min call on Wed 2/18 at 11:00 AM PT to walk the MAP and finalize dates.

If Wed doesn't work, propose two alternate times and we'll adjust.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Strategic Deals, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP proposal — Helix capacity & acceptance timeline

Quick sizing notes and risk flags (adding to the MAP draft):

Sizing math (ballpark)
- 1 A100 @ 512 tokens ~ 2.5–3.5 rps depending on model/quantization.
- Pilot 30 A100s -> ~75–105 rps baseline.
- Prod 100 A100s -> ~250–350 rps baseline; H100s reduce GPU count by ~2x for identical throughput but increase lead time and cost per unit.

Recommendation: start with a 2-tranche approach
- Tranche A (T+6 weeks): 40 A100s (pilot validation + performance tuning).
- Tranche B (T+10–12 weeks): remaining capacity to reach 100 A100s or equivalent H100 conversion if Helix prefers denser H100 pool.

Risk / mitigation
- Lead-time sensitivity: H100-based Dedicated commits are efficient at runtime but can add procurement friction; recommend A100-first pilot for speed.
- Compliance gating: SOC2 evidence can slow acceptance; propose parallel run of evidence collection during pilot to avoid blocking tranche 1.

Attachment: gpu-sizing-model.xlsx (workbook with throughput scenarios).

I'll join the Wed 11am PT MAP call and prepare a short slide with run-rate economics per tranche.

—Ben
